paper_sections.title: Estimating effective connectivity in Alzheimer's disease progression: A dynamic causal modeling study

description.value: The study estimated resting-state effective connectivity among default mode, salience, and central executive network regions in cognitively normal, early mild cognitive impairment, late mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease groups, and examined group differences and associations with MMSE and CDR scores.

design.value: A secondary analysis of longitudinally documented and publicly available ADNI-2 resting-state fMRI data from four stable progression-stage groups. Region-level time series were entered into dynamic causal modeling, group connectivity was inferred with parametric empirical Bayes and Bayesian Model Reduction, and connectivity strengths were compared using ANOVA and linear regression.

description.value: The MMSE score was used as a clinical and neuropsychological measure; group values were reported in Table 1 and the score was used as an outcome in linear regression.
The CDR score was used as a clinical measure of dementia severity; group values were reported in Table 1 and the score was used as an outcome in linear regression.

task_description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence. During the fMRI scans, all participants were instructed to keep their eyes open and relax.

instructions.value: Keep their eyes open and relax.

stimuli.value: No task stimulus was presented; stimulus u is usually set to zero in resting state models.

description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence (EPI). Each series has 140 volumes, and each volume consists of 48 slices of image matrices with dimensions 64 × 64. The flip angle was 80 degrees.

The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded to allow for participant stabilization and magnetic field equilibration. The remaining 130 volumes were corrected for the staggered order of slice acquisition. Preprocessing also included regression of head motion parameters, realignment for head movement, and spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

steps.value: The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded.

model_settings.value: The DCM comprised a neuronal model and an observation model. The neuronal model represented intrinsic connectivity, extrinsic connectivity, and input using the parameters θ = {A, B_j, C}; the observation model represented changes in BOLD signal through blood volume and deoxyhemoglobin content. For resting state, stimulus u was usually set to zero.

A parameter vector was sampled from a prior distribution, a random effect was added for each subject, data were generated using the DCM with observation noise, and calculated connection strengths were accompanied by the likelihood of each connection. The PEB process estimated group effective connectivity at five levels of confidence.

BMR was used to control the switching on and off of each connection by calculating the likelihood with the connection's presence and absence and estimating the parameter to infer the connectivity pattern.
The connectivity strengths for each subject group were compared using ANOVA. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.

A forward step-wise linear regression tested whether resting-state connectivity predicted MMSE scores. For CDR, both forward and backward connections between L-dlPFC and mPFC were predictive of the score.

estimator.value: forward step-wise linear regression; both forward and backward connections were tested for CDR
